newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha moves off lows despite weak crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha moves off lows despite weak crude.

text.p: The European naphtha market was firmer on Wednesday despite weakness across the rest of the oil complex, traders said.
"Naphtha's been held down for 10 days while crude was rallying. It's playing catch-up today while people are taking profits on crude," a dealer said.
June swaps were pegged $1.00 to $2.00 a tonne firmer at $185.50 to $186.50 with July 50 cents in contango.
Physical markets also looked firmer with one trading house bidding for a cargo of pipeline spec material at $185 a tonne cif NWE.
But traders noted that the illiquidity of the market left it open to manipulation and end-users were absent.
"The market is being driven by traders who have their own reasons for doing it," a dealer said.
Traders said the market was extremely thin with price levels highly variable depending on material specs and dates.
